newsitem.title: FRANCE: New car sales in France slide 33.6 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: New car sales in France slide 33.6 pct in January.

text.p: New car sales in France tumbled 33.6 percent last month from January 1996 levels, the French carmakers association CCFA said on Monday, adding that the drop reflected weakness in the market but also some distortions.
"This sharp drop confirms the trend observed since November 1996 when the effects of the expiry of the (state rebate programme) Prime Qualite began to be felt," the CCFA said in a statement.
New car sales, in provisional volume terms, totalled 122,552 last month, compared with 184,541 in January 1996.
The CCFA said the January 1996 figure was bolstered by a spurt in sales following the disruption caused by three weeks of public transport strikes in November and December of 1995.
A CCFA spokesman said January 1996 car sales were probably inflated by 20,000 units due to the spillover of 1995 orders.
Demand in January 1996 was also underpinned by a year-long new-cars-for-old government rebate programme that expired at the end of September 1996.
The French carmakers held 53.4 percent of the market last month, compared with 55.7 percent in January 1996.

The best performers were Volvo, whose car sales were 23 percent above year-earlier levels, and General Motors' Opel subsidiary, which saw a 10.7 percent sales drop -- the smallest among Europe's Big Six mass producers.
PSA Peugeot Citroen car sales plunged 43 percent to 29,829 units, while Renault SA sales fell 29.3 percent to 35,622 last month.
A spokeswoman at the Peugeot group said its sales were hit because the company, struggling to preserve its profit margins, resisted price cuts until mid-January.
"We saw everyone doing aggressive promotions, and we joined on January 15," the spokeswoman told Reuters.
Carmakers are engaged in a fierce price war in the French market that is especially harmful for the French manufacturers, which rely on domestic sales for their biggest profits.

Although the French government stopped offering rebates after September, some manufacturers including Ford and Fiat, are still giving discounts to buyers turning in old clunkers. Just about everyone is offering some kind of deal.
Industry officials are pressing the government to resume some sort of assistance. Sources at the Industry Ministry will say only that they are watching the market's evolution.
Shares in the PSA group were down 1.35 percent at 585 francs in early afternoon trade, while Renault shares were 0.25 percent lower, in line with the market's small decline.
